### 2026-10-29: # Chose parts

**1.5h**

# Chose parts

This was not a very complicated session. I had decided that i wanted to do something with video games, and eventually decided on a rhythm game.
I initially was looking at a board+display+some buttons for input. However, finding a good display was proving to be very hard, as most displays were too expensive for the budget.

_But then...._

I stumbled upon something really cool: the Cheap Yellow Display (CYD). It's basically a microcontroller with a display attached:

![entry1pic2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/aa25af0ed91067b1373b3c2c24e64a0bce02c74f4c16a2e8cd3559703f07f354.png)

and it is, as the name suggests, _cheap_. At around 15 bucks for one with a pretty decent size, it looked good. I looked around some more for CYD-adjacent boards and found the board i was going to use:

![entry1pic1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/55abddbb785353228b6cd48f457c577840f98f1557edc54b52e86315ec4ed246.png)

it has capacitive touch (the same thing a phone uses), so it's really nice for a rhythm game.

I then grabbed a battery and a speaker. I did stumble upon a little worry, when i saw that the draw current for the board seemed to be higher than what my battery could provide, so i looked around, and it turned out to be ok (i am going to double check tmrw tho i dont want my battery destroying everything on me). Now, i have to program the code (hopefully it fits within flash -- i dont want to  mess with sd cards)

### 2026-11-01: # Planned out my code!

**2.5h**

# Planned out my code!
# Finished the Level Builder!

This session, I planned out the overall structure of my code. The rhythm game I'm building is going to be kind of similar to Osu!, which is a point and click rhythm game:

![entry2pic3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/7b2b1212ff4ae245aa3d1dcbee98661265c472a963ec88cec36f89ea8899435b.png)

it fits perfectly with the strengths of the touchscreen and means i don't have to focus on art, which is extremely helpful.

My structure is mostly copied from this [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9XcLoEVnjrA):

It has:
- an input (touch detection in my case)  - will record where on screen the input is and at what time it was at
- music player- this will play music (and sound effects if i decide to add them)
- timer/metronome - will coordinate with music player to say where we are in the track
- level builder - since my game will have fixed levels, this will be me
- validator - checks player actions using the level, and timer (with some error margins)
 - display - shows the results of all of this

today i finished a program for the level builder. This will let me more easily make stuff than hand typing in x-y coords and timing

I just made a simple java application because its sunday and i dont have the time to learn anything else -_- :

![entry2pic1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/cb40dcb85be3fc616b5d9a4ebf26efa97f87c60247510043a3627de11cb09364.png)

this will be run on your computer and then the file it generates will be flashed to the microcontroller.

Some images of it working:

![entry2pic4](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Txtz56AlpXYSvJEhT04HAEIaAgIKQaYV/246581b64e6386babf91b5f78791d11d60b8d62fa04f6fe7b2e09feb6402acf7.png)

_it doesnt look the best but it works so that's all that matters im running out of time lololol_
